articleTitle: A High Gain and High CMRR Instrumentation Amplifier for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, an instrumentation amplifier (IA) based on operational amplifiers (op-amps) for biomedical applications is presented. Such IA achieves high gain and high common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR) while maintaining low power consumption, high power supply rejection ratio (PSRR) as well as other design constraints. The IA uses three identical two-stage telescopic cascode op-amps at the input and output stages. The feedback networks are comprised of resistors and capacitors, which are different from those in conventional voltage mode IA. The resistive feedback is utilized in the input stage to increase the stability while the capacitive feedback is employed in the output stage to filter undesired frequency components and enhance the gain of the IA. The schematic of IA is designed and simulated under 180 nm CMOS technology using Cadence Spectre tool. The gain and CMRR of the single op-amp are 100.45 dB and 94.8 dB respectively. The power consumed by each op-amp is 12.96 μW at a supply voltage of ± 0.9 V. RC Miller compensation technique helps the op-amp reaching a phase margin of 60°. This IA consumes a power of 38.88 μW and CMRR of 147.68 dB, with a gain of 101.61 dB. The proposed technique is suitable for a variety of biomedical applications due to its high gain and high CMRR.

articleTitle: Implementation of LSTM Accelerator for Speech Keywords Recognition
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The speech keyword detection system is generally used to detect a specific wake-up word spoken by the user, as a simple interactive command between the user and the device, or a front end of a larger voice recognition system for determining whether to open a large speech recognition system at the back end. Yet, such keyword recognition systems are always active, hence have strict power and latency constraints. This paper proposes an implementation of an LSTM accelerator based on an iterative linear approximation scheme, which optimizes the circuit implementation while maintaining high accuracy and reliability. The scheme of this paper has been verified on the FPGA board, and real-time speech recognition power consumption is only less 150$\mu$w.

articleTitle: A Broad-Band 1:4 Static Frequency Divider MMIC in InPHBT
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper design and realize a broad-band 1:4 static frequency divider MMIC in 0.7$\mu$m InGaAs/InP DHBT technology. It is realized in a complete circuit structure and can be directly used in high precision instruments and relative systems to replace divide modules. Test results show that it can operate from 1GHz to 48GHz with sine-wave input. The input power dynamic range is from -10 to 10 dBm during the whole bandwidth. The output power is all above 0dBm and the SSB phase noise is -141.15dBc/Hz at 24GHz input.

articleTitle: A Novel Authorization Methodology to Prevent Counterfeit PCB/Equipment through Supply Chain
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In modern semiconductor supply chain, the problem of counterfeit IC and PCB/equipment is getting more and more attention. Previous works mainly focus on detecting counterfeit IC. In this paper, a novel authorization methodology to prevent counterfeit PCB/equipment through supply chain is brought forward. A ring oscillator array is inserted into the selected IC, and by judging whether the periods of ROs in the resonant and non-resonant state of the PCB matche the database from the authentic ones, the counterfeit PCB/equipment can be detected. The proposed authorization structure has been implemented on some authentic and counterfeit FPGA development boards, and more than 90% counterfeit PCBs can be identified by a 2-class support vector machine (SVM) classifier.

articleTitle: A 12bit 16MS/s Asynchronous SAR ADC with Speed-Enhanced Comparator and TSPC Latch
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: this paper presents a 12bit 16MS/s asynchronous successive approximation register analog-to-digital converter (SAR ADC) with a speed-enhanced comparator and true single-phase-clock (TSPC) latch. An additional positive feedback loop is applied to the comparator to increase the comparator speed. Moreover, the use of TSPC latch reduces the load on the comparator and decreases the delay of the SAR LOGIC to the DAC. This paper also introduces a method of implementing a variable delay unit. The proposed ADC was simulated in SMIC one-poly-eight-metal (1P8M) 130nm CMOS technology. At a 3.3V supply, the ADC achieves an SNDR of 70.8dB and consumes 4.95mW. The peak DNL error is +0.25/-0.25LSB, and the peak INL is +1.1/ -0.8LSB.

articleTitle: A Low-Noise, Low-Power, and Chopper-Stabilized, Current-Feedback Instrumentation Amplifier for Current Sensing Application
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a low-noise, low-power, and chopper-stabilized current-feedback instrumentation amplifier (CFIA) for current sensing application. To achieve high common-mode-rejection ration (CMRR), the CFIA employs a three-stage topology with nested-Miller compensation. Through chopping both the input and intermediate stages of the amplifier, an input-referred noise power spectral density (PSD) of 22.7 nV/$\sqrt{}$Hz is achieved at 3 mHz. To reduce chopper ripple, the amplifier employs a continuous time AC-coupled ripple reduction loop. The proposed amplifier is implemented in a SMIC 0.18-$\mu$m CMOS process, the CFIA shows a simulated CMRR of 130 dB at a supply voltage of 3.3 V with a current of 200 $\mu$A.

articleTitle: A Low Computational Complexity Method of PTS
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The main drawback of OFDM system is the large PAPR(peak to average power average). PTS(partial transmission sequence) as a traditional method of reducing PTS has a huge computational complexity, in this paper, we proposed a trade-off method with suboptimal performance but much lower computational complexity than traditional method, we called it Spacing-PTS. This method mainly used homogenized algorithm, it works better than traditional trade-off method.

articleTitle: A New Generation of Static Timing Analysis Technology Based on N7+ Process—POCV
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: With the continuous development of semiconductor technology, timing analysis is becoming more and more complicated. Static timing analysis is constantly improving the constraint mode. The traditional on-chip variation (OCV) has become increasingly unsatisfactory under advanced technology. The design requirements of the tens of millions of high-speed chips; the advanced on-chip methodology (advanced OCV, AOCV), while solving the pessimism of the traditional method, will increase the analysis time. This article will introduce the new generation of static timing analysis technology applied in the 7Plus process - Parametric on-chip variation (POCV); POCV simulates the delay distribution probability obtained by the variation in a certain case, which is more accurate than AOCV. And reduce the time of timing analysis, increasing the number of iterations of timing analysis.

articleTitle: An Efficient VLSI Design of Residue to Binary Converter Circuit for a New Moduli Set {22n, 22n–1 – 1, 22n–1 + 1}
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a new 6n bit moduli set {2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n</sup>, 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n-1</sup> - 1, 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n-1</sup> + 1}, n ≥ 2 with its associated Residue representaion to binary representation arithmetic scheme. After demonstrating that the proposed moduli set is valid for the construction of a Residue Number System Processor, a reverse converter algorithm is presented using the New Chinese Remainder Theorem (CRT) I. Closed forms of multiplicative inverses required for the implementation of the New CRT I are introduced. The resulting architecture is further reduced to obtain an adder based and memory free scheme. Our investigations after implementing the proposed converter and other best known similar state of the art schemes on Xilinx xc6slx45-3fgg484 FPGA shows that on the average, the converter circuit for the new moduli set {2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n</sup>, 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n-1</sup> - 1, 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n-1</sup> + 1} is more efficient than other similar state of the arts converters in terms of area resource requirement and conversion time.

articleTitle: A Novel Low-Noise Bandgap Reference with an Active RC Filter
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A high-area efficiency and low-output noise bandgap reference (BGR) circuit is proposed in this study. Compared with the passive low-pass RC filter with a large-area capacitor in conventional BGR circuit, an active low-pass RC filter with a significantly area-efficiency capacitor and a large equivalent resistor is proposed in this study, where the large equivalent resistor is achieved by using an ultra-low-power currentmirror circuit. Due to the proposed active filter, BGR circuit with an output capacitor of just 10 pF obtains the similar noise flowing compared with the traditional BGR circuit using a passive filter with an output capacitor of 1000 pF. The proposed BGR circuit implemented in a standard 0.5-μm CMOS process and with a total current of 14 μA at a supply voltage of 5 V, shows an output reference voltage of 1.25 V, a temperature coefficient (TC) of 5 ppm/ °C with a temperature range from - 40-125°C, and an approximate squared output noise as low as 1.45E - 14 V<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/Hz when the frequency is higher than 5 kHz.

articleTitle: Divide-By-3 Dual-Resonance Injection-Locked Frequency Divider
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A dual-resonance injection-locked frequency divider (ILFD) is proposed to perform the function of divide-by-3 by using a single-ended injection. The dual-resonance LC resonator is consisted of a parallel-tuned LC resonator in shunt with a series resonant LC tank. The ILFD has been implemented with the TSMC 90 nm CMOS technology and the core power consumption is 4.278 mW at the dc drain-source bias of 0.6 V. At the input power of 0 dBm, the low-frequency band and high-frequency band divide-by-3 operation ranges are respectively from 13.27 GHz to 15.24 GHz and 29.3 GHz to 31.4 GHz.

articleTitle: Divide-by-2 Transformer-Based Injection-Locked Frequency Dividers with Two Active Cores
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This letter presents a high-performance wide-band divide-by-2 injection-locked frequency divider (ILFD) in the 0.18 μm CMOS process. The ILFD uses transformer-coupled resonator with two resonant frequencies based on the lumped inductor model, and it consists of two sub-ILFDs coupled by inductive coupling. The sub-ILFD can be switched on/off to aid the circuit analysis, thus the ILFD can operate in three modes. At low input power, the two sub-ILFDs act as an independent ILFDs with a high-band locking range and a low-band locking range. At high input power, the ILFD has two non-overlapped locking ranges indicating that the dual-resonance resonator plays the role and will lead to a wide overlapped locking range. At the power consumption of 1.83 mW and at the input power of 0 dBm, the low-band locking range is 3.3 GHz from 2.3 to 5.6 GHz. The optimal bias condition at low power yields wide locking range and high figure of merit. Measurement data shows the designed ILFD has employed the property of a dualresonance resonator.

articleTitle: A Practical Estimation of Periodic Power Supply Induced Jitter for Clock Buffer Chains
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a simple but practically accurate analytical closed-form expression for estimation of periodical power supply induced jitter (PSIJ) in MOS clock buffer chains. The closed-form expression is algebraically simple requiring only a few circuit simulation results without the pre-knowledge of circuit SPICE parameters. The expression predicts MOS clock buffer's period PSIJ and N-Cycle PSIJ. Compared to SPICE simulated jitter, the closed-form expression predicts PSIJ with a maximum +30% error, which is generally sufficient for early-stage clock-buffer jitter budgeting before circuit implementations. The expression can be hand calculated and is well suited for IC design and application engineers to quickly summarize jitter tolerances for clock distribution networks in high-speed PHYs such as DDRs and SERDESes.

articleTitle: A 433MHz Transmitter Based on Injection-Locking and Frequency Multiplication
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In recent years, the MICS band has become more and more versatile, and at the same time, the power consumption issue of the transmitter has been plaguing people. We designed a highly integrated 433 MHz MICS band transmitter which is based on cascaded multi-phase injection locking and frequency multiplication to enable low power operation. The transmitter is designed with the TSMC 180-nm CMOS process. The core area of the transmitter is only 0.0018 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. This structure consumes a total power of 0.58mW and outputs -28dBm power on 50 Ω load. It is fully integrated except for the crystal and the matching network.

articleTitle: Memory optimization of CNN Heterogeneous Multi-Core Architecture
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Convolutional neural networks(CNNs) computing complexity raises challenges to the power and cost of CNN accelerators. The power consumption and delay of the data access between on-chip and off-chip memories have been a bottleneck of the on-chip system for CNN acceleration. We propose a static scheduling framework based on our heterogeneous programmable multi-core ASIP (Application Specific Instruction-set Processor) for inference of deep learning. This scheduling framework minimizes power consumption and promotes performance under the hardware resource limitation, including datapath computing capability, access bandwidth limitation, and on-chip memory size. We also discussed how to achieve theoretical maximum performance for a set of fixed hardware constraints. Comparing to the scheduling on DNA(deep neural architecture) under the same AlexNet platform, our scheduling achieves 11.8% more average resource utilization. By reusing and broadcasting local data, the average DRAM access of our design is reduced down to 41% of the access of DNA. The estimated power consumption of this design is 35% lower than the power of DNA, mostly because of the power reduction from DDR data accesses. Meanwhile, through the ping-pang memory and the careful design of data partition, the time of data access between DRAM and SRAM is reduced 77% by access hidden.

articleTitle: A Laser Modulation Driver in 130-nm CMOS Technology for Quantum Key Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Laser modulation is a process to modulate the photons to different states in quantum key distribution (QKD) system. A laser modulation driver, which is a pre-driver for the laser modulator, is presented in this paper. The laser modulation driver is implemented in a 130-nm complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) process. The laser modulation driver can provide a current pulse signal with an adjustable amplitude and an adjustable pulse-width to a distributed power amplifier. The pulse-width of the current signal can be adjusted from 300 ps to 3800 ps, the maximum adjustable amplitude is 14.4 mA, and the data rate can reach 625 Mb/s. According to the test results, the laser modulation driver can meet the requirements of the electro-optic modulator (EOM) in QKD system, and it can be used in the laser modulation circuit in QKD experiments.

articleTitle: An optimized Low-Complexity Barzilai-Borwein Algorithm for Signal Detection in Massive MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Detection of signals in massive MIMO systems is a challenging problem. While near-optimal detection can be realized by the minimum-mean-square-error (MMSE) and zero-forcing (ZF) algorithms, the applicability of these algorithms is greatly limited by the need for a large number of complex matrix inversion operations. In this paper, we propose a signal detection approach based on an optimized Barzilai- Borwein (BB) algorithm whose initialization is tuned using symmetric successive over-relaxation (SSOR). The theoretical and experimental results demonstrate that our approach has an order-of-magnitude lower complexity with no matrix inversion, a near-optimal better performance, and a highly accelerated convergence speed compared to the conventional SSOR-based methods. Besides, the detection performance of the ZF algorithm can be quickly approached by few iterations of our method.

articleTitle: A New Hardware Trojan Detection System Based on CRON
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: With the globalization of the IC design flow, ICs are exposed to malicious inclusion referred to as Hardware Trojans (HT) which are known great threat for many application such as military systems, financial infrastructures. Hardware Trojan detection has emerged as an important research domain. In this paper, we propose an integrated new system to detect HT, which is composed of an innovative detection circuit named concurrent ring oscillator network (CRON) based on ring oscillator network (RON), data analysis program, target circuit, and other auxiliary circuits. We implement the system on FPGA and the scenario is simulated when the circuit is attacked by active HT. We find the suitable data analysis approach with machine learning method and the results demonstrate that our system can detect Trojan which is activated from sleep state and give the target circuit enough safety guarantee with 98% detection rate.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Low Quiescent Current Output Capacitor-Less Low-Dropout Regulator with Dynamic Bias Circuit
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: An ultra-low quiescent current LDO regulator for micro-energy harvesting system is implemented in a standard 0.35 um CMOS process. By using an error amplifier with double differential input and a push-pull output stage architecture, the proposed LDO is able to operate at ultra low quiescent current. Adding dynamic bias circuit ensures that the system still has a good working condition over the entire load range. Detail analysis is given to explain its operating principle. Simulation results are presented for the proposed LDO. Load transient measurements show that the maximum overshoot and undershoot voltage are 63 and 79 mV respectively, while the line transient measurements show the output variation are within 50 mV in all circumstances. The quiescent current is only 900 n A at supply voltage of 2.3 V under the minimum load condition.

articleTitle: Numerical Study and Parametric optimization of Pin-Fin in the Microchannel Radiators with Hot Spots
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The uneven distribution of heat flux tends to form localized hot spots inside the chip. The presence of hotspots poses a new challenge for the thermal management of heat sinks and 3D chip stacks. In this paper, the effects of the transverse and longitudinal spacing of the staggered pin fin arrays on the wall temperature and pressure drop in chip were studied. The results show that, with decreasing the fin spacing, the pressure drop increases nonlinearly while the wall temperature decreases slightly. Furthermore, the transverse spacing and the longitudinal spacing of the microneedle fin were optimized by using the response surface approximation method. Compared with conventional microneedle fin heat sink, the maximum pressure drop of the optimized heat sink can be decreased by 25.47%.

articleTitle: A New Single-Port Five-Transistor SRAM Cell Design for Signal Processing Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Static random access memory (SRAM) has been widely used as the typical memory for logic LSIs due to its fast operations and a little power consumed at standby mode. In this paper, a new single-port five-transistor (5T) SRAM cell integrated with assist circuitries is proposed. This design is to provide an efficient solution to the writing `1' issue to improve write operations and to introduce a two-phase reading methodology to speed up reading speed and thereby avoiding unwanted power dissipation. Also, by using the standby startup circuit design, the SRAM cell can reduce leakage current in standby mode. Simulations are conducted to show the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A 220GHz GaAs Integration Nonlinear Transmission Line Frequency Doubler Based on Resistive Planar Schottky Diodes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A 25 μ m thick GaAs monolithic integrated nonlinear transmission line 220GHz frequency doubler is designed based on planar Schottky diodes in this paper. In order to improve the output power and bandwidth, a nonlinear transmission line (TLNL) structure is used to achieve frequency multiplication. Considering the influence of the passive structure of the diodes in the terahertz band, an electromagnetic model is established to obtain accurate diode parameters. Based on the model, the 220GHz frequency doubler has a peak frequency efficiency of 10% and a maximum output power of 20mW at an input power of 200mW. In the 185GHz-237GH band, the frequency multiplier efficiency is above 5%, and the output power greater than 10mW.

articleTitle: Application and Comparison of the Contactless Overvoltage Measurement System Based on Integrated Electro-Optic Sensors
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Effective monitoring of transient overvoltage is the key to field test, fault analysis and optimal design of power system. Traditional overvoltage measurement methods need to connect primary equipment to obtain signals, which is inconvenient and has security risks. A contactless overvoltage measurement system based on integrated electro-optic sensors (IEOSs) is introduced and applied in the field. The inductive electric field on IEOS is converted into optical signals with long-distance transmission and strong anti-interference ability. After modulation by the electric field to be measured, the phase difference information is carried into the photodetector and the output voltage of three-phase coupling is obtained. The measurement system has the advantages of no electrical connection with primary equipment, no additional power supply for sensors, wide frequency band and fast response. The coupling relationship of three-phase electric field is analyzed, and the decoupling strategy of output voltage waveform based on linear transformation is given. Finally, the field test results of this measurement system are compared with the waveforms recorded by the fault recorder, which verifies the effectiveness of the decoupling strategy. It also shows that the measurement system has good high frequency response characteristics.

articleTitle: A New Memory-Based Routing Policy for Mesh Network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: We propose a new routing policy in Network on Chip (NoC) which is based on Memory. Compared with the data-based routing policy, the Memory-based routing policy can carry larger data volumes among the network and performs better routing efficiency. In the data-based NoC routing policy, data is routed among the network, but when data volumes are actually beyond data volumes carried by the network, the routing capacity of NoC network will be greatly reduced, and data congestion in the network will be caused. This problem does not only greatly reduce the routing efficiency of NoC network, but also causes data congestion in the network. In NoC, Mesh network is the main direction due to its simple topology, predictable routing path and strong network scalability. Therefore, taking Mesh network as an example, we combined Memory with Mesh network to implement the data-based routing policy. We also verify our design with FPGA successful.

articleTitle: The Core Chip Design of Fast Locked All Digital Phase-locked Loop
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper introduces a counter-based ADPLL (all-digital phase-locked loop) calibration module. The reference frequency of the all-digital phase-locked loop is 100MHz, and a bandwidth-adjustable filter is used. The circuit is based on a 40nm CMOS process with an average lock time of 1.2 μs.

articleTitle: Study on the Effect of Liquid Cooling on the Temperature Distribution of Diesel Engine ECU
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, an ECU simulation model of some kind of domestic diesel engine is established by using FloTHERM to study the effect of liquid cooling on ECU temperature distribution. Diesel is used as coolant in this paper. By changing the flow rate and temperature of the coolant, several comparative analyses were carried out, and it was found that the cooling effect of the liquid varied with the flow rate and temperature. The results show that liquid cooling can effectively reduce the temperature of ECU. Moreover, within the given range, the cooling effect increases with the increase of the flow rate, but the increase rate gradually decreased. And the temperature of ECU decreases linearly with the decrease of coolant temperature.

articleTitle: Electrical Locating Technology for Failure Point Location Based on an Amplifier Module
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A boom in microsystem modules has brought with it increasingly integrated internal chips that are smaller and smaller in feature size. Meanwhile, multilayer wiring has also got more complicated. Consequently, locating failure points in these chips - a crucial link in module failure analysis technologies - is becoming even harder, through electrical methods or otherwise. This article revolves around a type of amplifier module suffering a failure. Alongside traditional failure analysis methods, electrical techniques of infrared hotspot, isolation testing and surface delayering are employed to successfully diagnose the failure, including the location and appearance of the failure point. Findings in this article are hoped to facilitate future development of internal electrical locating technologies for module failure analysis.

articleTitle: A 71.8-87.9 GHz CMOS Injection-Locked Frequency Divider with Coupled Inductance
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a technique of inductor coupling is used to optimize the bandwidth of the injection-locked transformer. This design replaces the inductance of a conventional injection-locked divider with a transformer consists by two coupled inductance, each has its own independent cross-coupled pair. This design is based on 40nm-CMOS technology, with a supply voltage of 0. 9V, the post-simulation results achieve a locking range of 71.8-87.9GHz with an injected signal of 0dBm, and the core chip size is 88$\times $1301$\mu \mathrm{m}^{2}$.

articleTitle: A 10 GHz CMOS Active Phase Shifter with Pole-Splitting All-Pass Quadrature Generator
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A 8-bit 10GHz active phase shifter (PS) is presented in this paper. The architecture is based on the all-pass quadrature generator and vector sum active PS. A pole splitting technique is proposed to extent the operational bandwidth. The PS saved voltage headroom and decreased the time constant of the system by removing stacked switches. The proposed PS is designed in TSMC 65nm GP CMOS technology, dissipating 8.4 mW from a 1.2 V supply with the quadrature input signals at 10 GHz. It achieves a gain of 1.8-2.2 dB from the frequency of 7-11 GHz. The simulated NF is around $\lt8.3$ dB with all process corners. The phase error is less than 2.5°.

articleTitle: Optimum Design of a New High Voltage Cascaded Amplifier Based on OPA454
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In order to obtain high linearity voltage signal with adjustable frequency, an optimal design scheme of high voltage cascaded linear amplifier based on OPA454 is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the main circuit, isolation circuit and cascade amplifier circuit of the high voltage cascade amplifier are designed. Then, the negative feedback characteristics and capacitive load characteristics of the linear amplifier are analyzed to ensure the high linearity and capacitive load capability of the output voltage signal. Finally, a two-stage cascade amplifier circuit model is built and tested in time domain at 0.001 Hz, 1.0 Hz and 1.0 kHz. The frequency response curves of the first-stage voltage amplifier circuit and the two-stage voltage amplifier circuit are compared in the frequency domain. The results show that the output voltage waveform of the new linear amplifier can be linearly amplified by 40n times of the input voltage, which achieves high linearity and low waveform distortion. It meets the requirement of accurate voltage amplification under adjustable frequency.

articleTitle: Influence of the Interface Charges' Location on the Threshold Voltage of TFT
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: With the development of VLSI (Very Large Scale Integration), the size of devices decreases and the electric field of gate oxide increases relatively. The degradation of TFT (Thin Film Transistor) devices is further affected by NBTI effect. When the device DB-NBTI degenerates, interface charges distribution is non-uniform. In this paper, the gate of p-type silicon TFT device is divided into several grid segments, and different concentration of interface charges is introduced to simulate the non-uniform distribution of charge. The relationship between the interface charges' location and the threshold voltage is well simulated numerically, in which the conditions of drain biasing, interface charges' concentration and with or without traps are considered. It is found that the device transfer characteristics lag behind those without considering the trap model. The influence of non-uniform interface charges on the threshold voltage of TFT is stronger near the source and weaker near the drain. When the drain voltage increases, the influence is suppressed to some extent. At the same time, the influence of interface charges on pMOS and TFT are compared and analyzed. The proposed work can promote the research on Drain Bias-Negative Bias Temperature Instability (DB-NBTI) effect.

articleTitle: A Synchronous Rectifier Energy Collection Circuit with Two Energy-Transfer Schemes for A 65% Power Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This study presents an efficient and self-startup energy harvesting circuit consisting of two energy-transfer schemes. One energy-transfer scheme is based on a transformer, and the other energy-transfer scheme is based on a boost converter. At the same time, a new and improved rectification architecture is adopted. The MOS transistor is used to replace the diode, which greatly reduces the rectification loss, so that the circuit can achieve higher efficiency. The final output is stabilized by a negative feedback circuit, and the output voltage is stabilized at 2V. The design is implemented by the use of 0.4 um BCD process. With the minimum input voltage is 50 mV, maximum efficiency of 65% can be achieved.

articleTitle: Analysis of Squeeze Film Air Damping with Lattice Boltzmann Method in Transition Regime
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The study of squeeze film damping (SFD) under large Knudsen number is of great significance for the design of MEMS devices. The Reynolds equation based on the continuum hypothesis is no longer applicable due to the small size. In this paper, the Lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) is used to simulate the SFD of rectangular cantilever in transition regime. The quality factor obtained is compared with the values of Monte Carlo model, Reynolds equation model, and experiments. The results show that the LBM model has a better accuracy in the simulation of SFD in transition regime.

articleTitle: A Digitally Controlled CMOS Analog Baseband Circuit with Low Noise for 7681GHz Automotive Radar
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a digitally controlled CMOS analog baseband (ABB) circuit with low noise for 76-81GHz automotive radar, implemented in CMOS 65nm GP technology. The ABB consists of two high pass filters, two programmable gain amplifiers, one low pass filter, and one buffer. As a part of the receiver, ABB provides 42dB dynamic gain range and reconfigurable bandwidth from 100 kHz/ 200 kHz/ 1 MHz/ 5 MHz to 2 MHz/ 5 MHz/ 10 MHz/ 20 MHz. The entire configuration is digitally controlled by SPI. The typical noise Figure of the receiver is 10.2dB without ABB, 15.3dB with ABB at minimum gain, and 12.2dB with ABB at maximum gain. The ABB occupies a chip area of 1.620*0.445 (mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) without pad and consumes 24mA current. The peak-to-peak differential output voltage of ABB is up to 2V.

articleTitle: Design For Test of Radiation-Hardened SOC
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: At present, with the rapid development of space application technology, the radiation capability of SOC in space equipment is becoming more and more important. This brings new challenges to the Design For Test (DFT) design of radiation-hardened SOC. This paper introduces the DFT design method of a radiation-hardened SOC. This method can not only test the output of all registers and Static Random Access Memory (SRAM) cells when SOC is exposed to radiation sources, but also test the storage results of Triple Modular Redundancy (TMR) or Error Detection And Correction (EDAC) cells separately. The DFT design has been applied to radiation experiments and wafer test of radiation-hardened SOC, which greatly improves the test efficiency.

articleTitle: Thermoelastic Damping in Bilayered Microbeam Resonators with Annular-cross Section
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The design of high quality factor (Q-factor) resonator requires consideration of thermoelastic damping (TED), which is an internal energy dissipation mechanism and determines the upper limit of the Q-factor. The previous works of TED models for microbeams mainly focus on the microbeams with rectangular or circular cross-section. Thus, there is a lack of study aiming at the microbeam with annular cross-section. In this paper, a TED model for the bilayered microbeam with annular cross-section is proposed on basis of Zener's theory and Green function method. The constraints of microbeam is cantilevered and excited by axial sinusoids. The results calculated by the present model agree well with those obtained by the finite element method (FEM) model, proving the validity of predicting TED values for bilayered microbeam.

articleTitle: Research on Fault Prediction Method of Analog Circuits Based on DCQGA-SVR
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Aiming at the shortcomings of analog circuit fault prediction technology, the DCQGA-SVR analog circuit fault prediction method is proposed. Firstly, the failure mechanism of electrolytic capacitor and power MOSFET in analog circuit is analyzed. The fault parameters that can be used to reflect circuit fault, map electrolytic capacitor and power MOSFET are researched. The average output power is extracted as the characteristic parameter of circuit fault. Secondly, the double-chain quantum genetic algorithm is used to optimize the support vector machine regression algorithm to predict the fault feature parameters, and then the fault prediction model is established. Finally, the Boost circuit is used as the simulation test circuit, and compared with the traditional QGA-SVR algorithm and LS-SVM algorithm. The results show that the proposed prediction method has small mean square error and can effectively predict the fault.

articleTitle: The Influence of Working and Protective Grounding on Submarine Cable in AC Withstand Voltage Test
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The grounding technique is one of the important measures to protect the personal safety and reliable operation of electricity equipment in electric power system. Nowadays, the protection grounding, working grounding and lightning protection grounding are widely used in high voltage equipment. This paper is based on 500kV XLPE insulated submarine cable in Zhoushan transmission project. In order to get the influence of working and protective grounding on submarine cable in AC voltage withstand voltage test, theoretical analysis and experimental application are combined to analyze. The advantages and disadvantages of independent grounding and also common grounding are discussed in this paper. The results show common grounding fully meets the long submarine cable line AC withstands voltage test requirements.

articleTitle: A 50 GHz High Sensitivity InP HBT Comparator
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a high speed and high sensitivity voltage comparator circuit is designed based on the 0.7um InP double heterojunction bipolar transistor technology with a current gain cutoff frequency (f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sub>) of 320 GHz. The comparator consumes 410mW with a single 3.3V power supply. The simulation results show that the input sensitivity is 1mV with 25GHz data input and 3mV with 49GHz data input at 50GS/s. The input signal dynamic range of the comparator is 55.6dBc and the Figure of Merit (FoM) of the comparator is 1.99. To our best knowledge, it achieves the highest sensitivity and the highest value of FoM at 50GS/s.

articleTitle: Design of Automated Voltage Protection Circuit for Digital DC-DC Switching Power Supply Digital-analog Hybrid Integrated System Design
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Based on the research of digital DC-DC switching power management system, this paper uses arbitration scheduling circuit to perform segmental periodic overvoltage detection and undervoltage detection on the output voltage. When DPWM is ‘1’, overvoltage detection is turned on. When DPWM is ‘0’, undervoltage detection is turned on. This can reduce power consumption effectively. At the same time, on the basis of this, the detection signal is reported to the CPU for diagnosis. When the output voltage signal is wrong, the CPU will shut off the power supply of the entire system to achieve the purpose of automatic voltage protection. The new circuit structure proposed in this paper has the characteristics of low power consumption compared with the traditional analog circuit structure, and can realize the information interaction with the CPU to achieve precise logic control. Finally, the simulation was carried out using the 0.18um BCD process, and the ideal results were obtained.

articleTitle: A Portable Fault Location Device for High Voltage Equipment Based on Acoustic Wave Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Abnormal vibration sounds often occur in the operation of high-voltage power equipment. The main reason is that the busbar joints, insulator fixtures and other parts are caused by electromagnetic force due to loosening of the screw. In order to find the fault point quickly, it is necessary to locate the fault location of high-voltage equipment in operation. Acoustic wave fault location technology for portable high-voltage equipment can accurately measure the location information of abnormal sound fault point by using pickup electret and ultrasonic distance sensor. After practical use, it meets the requirements of patrol inspection and detection of power supply companies. It is of great significance to improve rapid maintenance and ensure power supply.

articleTitle: A Real-Time Fast Path Network Processor for EtherCAT and Home Gateway
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Network processors, also called protocol processors, are much used in mobile communications, broadband communications, and last mile accesses. Network processors are usually divided into fast path modules and slow path processors. Traditional fast path network modules are implemented as a configurable ASIC (Application Specific Integrated Circuit) with limited flexibility. In this paper, we designed and implemented a flexible fast path programmable network processor for EtherCAT real-time applications. The designed processor can also be used as fast path processors for home gateways being used up to 10GPON accesses. The processor is designed as an ASIP (Application Specific Instruction-set Processor) and it can be programmed for Ethernet, EtherCAT, IPv4, IPv6, UDP, and ARP. We are currently programming it to adapt to 5G layer two. The main contribution from the paper includes a fast path instruction set and its architecture. The performance of our instruction set is estimated more than 13 times faster than that of a single scaling general MCU.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Low Noise Capacitive Readout Circuit for Gyroscopes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Based on a continuous time voltage sensing, this paper presents an ultra-low noise capacitive readout circuit for capacitive gyroscopes which has a capacitive signal varying from 0 to 0.3 pF and its frequency is ranged from 10 to 20 kHz. The readout circuit is implemented by a charge sensitive amplifier (CSA) with both input and output common feedback circuit. The signal modulation technique controlled by 1 MHz carrier clock is adopted to shift low-frequency capacitive signal to high frequency and significantly release design requirement of the CSA. The proposed capacitive readout circuit is implemented based on 0.18-μm CMOS process, and the simulation results show that the designed readout circuit at a fixed 3.3 V supply voltage and common-mode voltage of 1.5 V achieves a resolution as low as 0.03 aF/sqrt Hz@10 kHz.

articleTitle: Progress on Surface Charges of Insulating Materials and Modification Methods
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In HVDC transmission system, surface charges accumulate easily on the surface of insulating materials, which cause surface discharge and surface flashover. This phenomenon reduces the insulation performance of insulating materials and restricts the engineering application of HVDC transmission. The researches of surface charges on insulating materials and its suppression measures in DC system have become a hot research direction. According to the current research of surface charges characteristics, this paper systematically describes the source, accumulation characteristics and dissipation characteristics of surface charges. In order to further reduce the influence of surface charges on HVDC transmission system, this paper also discusses the surface modification methods of controlling surface charges.

articleTitle: A 10-bit 320MS/s Time-Interleaved SAR ADC with an Improved Binary-Scaled Recombination Weighting Capacitor Array
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a 10-bit 320MS/s time-interleaved successive approximation register (SAR) ADC designed for WLAN (Wireless Local Area Network) applications. An improved binary-scaled recombination weighting capacitor array is disclosed in this work. The proposed SAR ADC achieves a SNDR of 59.9dB and an ENOB of 9.66 with Nyquist frequency at 1.2V and 320MS/s. The power dissipation is 2.2mW and the ADC core only occupies an area of 0.031mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> in 40nm CMOS process.

Author Keywords: improved binary-scaled recombination weighting capacitor array

articleTitle: A Frequency Adaptive Quasi-Synchronous Algorithm Applied to Digital Electric Energy Meters
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The input signal of digital electric energy meters is the sampling value message from electronic transformers. As the sampling frequency is fixed, spectrum leakage and fence effect will inevitably happen when sampling period is out of sync with signal period, thus leading to measurement error of electrical parameters and metering error of electric energy. A frequency adaptive quasi-synchronous algorithm is proposed to reduce synchronization error and improve the operation speed of algorithm. The algorithm can be used in digital electric energy meters and be applied to other instances also, such as non-integer-period sampling instrument.

articleTitle: Research on Fault Excitation Technology of Smart Meters
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: When the voltage line of the smart meter is interrupted frequently, the emergency response capability of the hardware and software functions of the smart meter will be tested. The internal parameter setting, clock recording, metering performance and deduction function may be disordered. In order to test the emergency response capability and stimulate the potential failure of the smart meter, this paper designs a set of smart meter voltage response capability tests. Through the test, it is found that some manufacturers' smart meters have inaccurate measurement and communication interruption.

articleTitle: Study on the Influence of Different Locations of Land and Sea on Geomagnetic Induced Current Based on Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: It is of great significance to study the factors affecting the geomagnetically induced current (GIC) for evaluating the influence of geomagnetic storms on the stable operation of power system. The magnitude of the GIC is related to many factors, among which the location of land and sea is very important. In order to study the influence of different locations of land and sea on GIC, nine different locations of land and sea are established on the basis of Quebec layered earth model. The distribution of GIC in different locations of land and sea is calculated based on Finite Element Method. Besides, the potential difference between two points at the same location is compared, the effect of different locations of land and sea locations on GIC is obtained. This can provide theoretical support for explaining the impact of different locations of land and sea on GIC, and also provides reference for evaluating the impact of geomagnetic storms on grid operation.

articleTitle: Detection of Transformer Winding Fault with Oscillation Wave Signal Based on Time-Frequency Transform
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In order to further improve the reliability of the transformer winding state detection, a method for analyzing winding state is proposed by using winding oscillation wave. The oscillation wave is obtained from the transient excitation generated by switching’s action under high voltage direct current (HVDC). Based on the field test, the oscillatory wave signal is de-noised by continuous wavelet transform and then its time-frequency characteristics are analyzed. The image recognition method and the matrix similarity degree are introduced to quantify the time-frequency signal characteristic. The results show that the method has high testing efficiency, and the matrix similarity can not only reflect the repeatability and regularity of oscillation waves in different amplitude and from different output side, but also better reflect the difference of transformer phase-to-phase windings. This method provides a reference for the research of transformer winding deformation detection.

articleTitle: A Time-Interleaved 14-bit 500MS/s Charge-Domain ADC with Mix-signal Mismatch Calibration
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A two channel time-interleaved 14-bit 500MS/s charge domain pipelined ADC with mix-signal for-ground mismatch calibration method based on binary search is proposed. The offset and gain error mismatch between the two channels are calibrated in the mix-signal for-ground calibration. The 14-bit 500MS/s charge domain pipelined ADC is designed and realized in a 1P6M 0.18$\mu$m CMOS process. Test results show the 14-bit 500MS/s ADC achieves the signal-to-noise ratio of 69.8 dBFS and the spurious free dynamic range of 82.3dB, with 72.1MHz input at 500MS/s, while consumes the power consumption of 365mW.

articleTitle: Analysis of Partial Discharge Test of Transformer Caused by Excitation Transformer Fault
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Partial discharge refers to a discharge phenomenon in which a portion of a region is discharged due to an electric field and there is no breakdown between the applied voltage conductors in an operating state. For transformers above 110kV, the partial discharge test is an effective means and method for verifying the insulation level of the transformer. Due to the limitations of the field test conditions, the partial discharge test of the transformer generally adopts a low-voltage side compensation press and a method of inducing a test voltage level on the high-voltage side. The state of the test equipment directly determines whether the experimental results meet the standard requirements. In this paper, we analyze the situation that the excitation is self-discharged and then transmitted to the transformer of the test, which results in the test result not meeting the standard requirements. At the same time, the excitation is returned to the factory for disintegration, and the cause of the accident is analyzed to provide experience and support for future field tests. During partial discharge test of transformer, the amount of partial discharge caused by the failure of the test equipment is difficult to distinguish. This type of problem can only be avoided by regular maintenance of the test equipment or by applying a voltage rise to the equipment.

articleTitle: Design of a Power Randomization Circuit for Block Ciphers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: To improve the anti-Power Analysis Attack ability of Block Ciphers, we summarized the research status of anti-attack technology. Starting with Mask Technology, the concept of Random Interleaving is put forward and its key property is proved. Based on the basic method of inserting random number, a Power Randomization circuit structure is designed and applied to the AES-128 algorithm circuit as an example. Finally the design of this paper is verified from three aspects. The results show that the algorithm circuit with this structure can correctly complete the encryption function, the ability to resist Power Analysis Attack has been significantly improved, and the circuit performance is good.

articleTitle: A 402 ∼614 MHz CMOS Transceiver for IEEE 802.15.6 Wireless Body Area Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A 402 ∼614 MHz CMOS transceiver is proposed and designed in standard 0.18$\mu$m CMOS technology, complying with the IEEE 802.15.6 Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN) standard. A current-reused differential common-gate low noise amplifier (CG-LNA), a high precision image rejection active-RC complex filter, a four-stage programmable gain amplifier (PGA), a high linearity power amplifier (PA) and so on, are employed. The simulation results show that, within the desired bandwidth from 402 MHz to 614MHz, the input/output power reflection coefficients of less than -16dB, the receiver gain range of $38 \sim 87$ dB and the output 1 dB compression point of over 2.11dBm are achieved. From a single voltage supply of 1.8V, 8mW and 16mW are consumed by the receiver and the transmitter, respectively.

articleTitle: A 0.4-V 1.9 μ W Amplifier for Low Power Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This manuscript presents a fully differential amplifier with a supply of 0.4V for low power biomedical applications. It is designed in a $0.13 \mu \mathrm{m}$ CMOS technology with regular VT transistors. By employing a gate-body input class-AB output topology and novel local common-mode feedback, it achieves large output swing, less noise and fast speed, with low power consumption. It also obtains less current variation against supply variation, which is critical for improving battery duration especially for ultra-low-voltage (ULV) operation. Its robust performance against process and supply variations is also verified by extensive corner simulations. Simulation results indicate that this amplifier has an open loop DC gain of 51dB, a unity gain bandwidth of 1.95MHz and a phase margin of 74° with a load of 24pF//1.16M$\Omega$ at 0.4V supply. The power consumption of the amplifier is only $1.9 \mu \mathrm{W}$.

articleTitle: Steady-State Thermal Simulation of the InP HBT Device Heat Spreading in DAHI Chip
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper we analyzed the problem of thermal management in heterogeneous integration (InP HBT on CMOS). In this work because InP HBT chiplet is vertically stacked on the silicon chip, the heat from HBT devices can only be dissipated downward through the Si substrate. We performed 3-D finite element analysis to investigate the potential of thermal heterogeneous interconnect (THIC) as vertical heat spreader. The Diverse Accessible Heterogeneous Integration (DAHI) chip with the area of 2.7 $\times$ 2.3m m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is also analyzed by ANSYS. The simulation results show that THIC can effectively accelerate heat dissipation in DAHI chip, which will also improve the electric performance or reliability.

articleTitle: An Exynos4412-based Embedded Control System Design for Multi-Channel Upper Limb Motor Function Rebuilding and Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presented an embedded control system based on Samsung Exynos4412 processor. It is designed for multi-channel EMG-Bridge prototype. The advanced processor Exynos4412 is used in the embedded control system with a 7-inch TFT-LCD touch screen for more efficient user interaction and more user-friendly extensions. The stimulation pulse can be adjusted within the parameter range of the normal FES mode. The patient registration & login system based on radio-frequency identification (RFID) technology and the SQLite database-based patient information management system software are implemented to realize for saving patient's treatment information without re-adjusting the treatment parameters each time. The prototype has been validated by performing normal FES stimulation on one healthy subject.

articleTitle: A Low Noise Operational Amplifier With Cascode Frequency Compensation Technique for Voice Detection and Recognition
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper proposes a low noise operational amplifier for voice detection and recognition. The transistor level low noise technologies and the cascode frequency compensation are presented in this design. This work has been implemented in a 180 nm CMOS process and simulated with a 2 V power supply, a 200 kΩ resistive load and a 220 pF capacitive load. The proposed amplifier consumes an area of 282 fm x 332 fm and a total quiescent current of 109.258 μA. And it achieves a closed loop gain of 2.96205 dB, a unity gain frequency of 3.18 MHz with 40.2° phase margin and an input integrated noise of -109.585 dBV within 20 Hz - 20 kHz (an input referred noise at 1 kHz of 28.61 nV/sqrt(Hz)).

articleTitle: An Energy Allocation Method of Nodes in Energy Harvesting Distributed Detection System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In the distributed detection system with energy harvesting, the uncertainty of node energy makes the optimal allocation of sensing and communication energy a challenge. This paper analyzed the influence of sensing uncertainty and communication uncertainty on detection system performance. The joint optimization of single slot node energy between sensing and communication was carried out by Monte Carlo simulation. The energy allocation method of nodes with the highest detection probability received by fusion center was determined, which laid a foundation for the establishment of node energy management strategy.

articleTitle: A 8-12GHz 4-Element SiGe BiCMOS Multi-Function Chip for Phased Array Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a 4-element X-band multi-function chip(MFC) based on SiGe technology, which includes RF switches, low noise amplifier, power amplifier driver, attenuator, phase shifter, Power divider and digital beam forming. The traditional MFC is realized by GaAs process, which has the disadvantages of high cost and low integration. This design is based on SiGe process, which greatly reduces the cost of the chip and improves the integration. A series of techniques, such as on-chip temperature compensation, phase compensation and amplifier parallel peaking, are adopted to achieve better temperature characteristics, smaller attenuation additional phase shift and broadband characteristics. The test results show that the MFC works at 8-12GHz, RMS phase error is less than 3.5 degrees, attenuation additional phase shift is less than 3degrees, the RX gain and TX gain is 10dB and 3dB, respectively. The gain variation is less than 0.019dB/oC. The size of the chip contains pad is about 6mm*9mm.

articleTitle: Laser Study for DICE-based Registers in a Commercial 130nm Process Technology
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, DICE-based register with SET filter architecture was developed for examining the single event vulnerability of DICE-Flip/Flop. Five DICE-based shift register chains each comprised of 1000 flip-flops have been implemented in a commercial 130nm bulk CMOS process. Measured SEE immunity in laser testing, and test results are described. A threshold laser energy of about 0.73nJ at VDD = 1. 2 V under room temperature is demonstrated. And the statured cross section is about 2$\times 10^{-9}$cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/bit. The designed DICE-based Flip/Flop is immune to SEL in the laser testing. These testing results demonstrate that the designed DICE-based registers can be used for space applications.

articleTitle: A Module-Level Pipeline Implementation Based on Inter-Board Heterogeneous
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: With the internet of things, autonomous driving, and smart security rapid development, data growth puts higher and more urgent requirements on processor computing performance. A single chip is hard to meet the real-time computing requirements in many scenarios, so it is necessary to expand multiple chips. This paper proposes a module-level pipeline FPGA cluster structure based on inter-board heterogeneous. The method divides a single enormous task into multiple modules and running each module on different FPGA as the pipeline structure between boards. In addition, considering the impact of communication delay between boards, it is proposed to use the delay between development boards as a separate stage of the pipeline. In this way, we can minimize a stage's runtime of module level pipeline. In order to evaluate the calculate capacity of per hardware resource, the concept of resource conversion efficiency (RCE) is proposed. Experimental results of LeNet -5 neural network with the module-level pipeline structure design demonstrates that proposed method increased processing capacity and resource utilization efficiency. Compared with the method of sequential execution, the execution speed and RCE of the proposed method are increased by 46.1% and 84.7% respectively.
